claim_text: People following vegan diets who do not regularly consume reliable B12-fortified foods or supplements are at increased risk of inadequate vitamin B12 intake because unfortified plant foods are not reliable natural sources of active B12.
health_goal_or_outcome: Identify dietary patterns that may require a reliable vitamin B12 source.

population.age_range: All ages; requirements and clinical assessment vary.
population.sex_or_life_stage: Pregnancy and lactation require particular attention.
population.other_context: Assess fortified food labels, frequency and current supplement use.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Vitamin B12 from fortified foods or supplements; verify the actual form and amount on product labels.
comparator: Reliable fortified food/supplement source versus no reliable source.
evidence_summary: NIH ODS Vitamin B12 Health Professional Fact Sheet describes vegan diets as a risk context and identifies fortified foods and supplements as reliable sources.
limitations: Diet pattern does not diagnose biochemical deficiency.
Current supplement and fortified-food use may already meet needs.
Neurological symptoms or suspected deficiency require clinical assessment.
